title: Knowing When to Act
note: A ruler with the greater strength, setting out against his enemy, learns the time that suits the march.

couplets.plain: By day the crow beats the owl. Rulers who would beat their enemies need the right time.
couplets.pm: By day the crow beats the owl, which is stronger than it. In the same way, rulers who mean to overcome their enemies must have a fitting time, because without it strength is useless. The fitting time is when heat and cold are even and bring no sickness, when water and food are at hand, and when the army can march without hardship.

links.quote: Rulers who would beat their enemies
By day the crow beats the owl
links.reason: The crow beats the owl only by day: every creature has its hour, and so has a ruler.

couplets.plain: Acting in step with the season is a rope that ties good fortune down so that it can’t leave.
couplets.pm: For a ruler to act in keeping with the time is a rope that binds to him the wealth that stays with no one and always moves on. It means doing things without missing the moment. Since the work then succeeds, the wealth it brings never leaves.

links.quote: Acting in step with the season
a rope that ties good fortune down
links.reason: திரு, good fortune, is pictured as a restless thing that must be roped to stay.

couplets.plain: Is any task hard, if you have the means and know the time?
couplets.pm: Are there any tasks that can be called too hard for rulers, if they act with the tools to finish them and at the time to do them? The tools are the three powers and the four means. He names the tools to show that even with them the time is needed. All work is then easily done.

links.quote: if you have the means and know the time

couplets.plain: Even if you aim at the whole world, it will come into your hands, if you act with an eye to the time and the place.
couplets.pm: Even someone who means to rule the whole world alone will have it in his hands, if he does what it takes knowing the time and suiting the place. What can’t be grasped comes within his grasp.

links.reason: Where you act counts along with when you act.

couplets.plain: Those who have their eye on the world stay still, unshaken, and watch for the time.
couplets.pm: Rulers who mean to take the whole world without fail don’t count on their greater strength. They look only for the fitting time, and until it comes they won’t march on the enemy. If they march anyway, both kinds of their greatness shrink and they suffer. Staying still is the one of the six courses of a ruler that is opposed to marching.
couplets.note: கலங்காது can go with the waiting, unshaken, or, as he takes it, with the aim, without fail.

links.reason: Those who aim at the whole world stay still and watch for the time.
While the moment is unclear, the counsel is to stay still and keep watching, unshaken.

couplets.plain: When a person of spirit holds back, it is like a fighting ram drawing back to charge.
couplets.pm: When a ruler of great strength doesn’t march but sits watching for the time, it is like a fighting ram stepping back so that it can leap and destroy its enemy. As the ram draws back to charge, the ruler holds back to win.

links.quote: When a person of spirit holds back
a fighting ram drawing back to charge

couplets.plain: The wise don’t flare up outwardly on the spot. They watch for the time and burn within.
couplets.pm: When enemies overstep, wise rulers don’t show anger at once where the enemy can see it. They learn the time that suits their victory and stay angry inside until it comes. If they show anger, the enemy guards himself. If they let the anger go, they can’t stop him overstepping again.

links.quote: watch for the time and burn within

couplets.plain: When you see your enemies, carry them. When you see their end, they will fall head first.
couplets.pm: Rulers who mean to win should bow low whenever they see their enemies, until the enemies’ last days come. Seeing this, the enemies neglect to guard themselves, and when the time comes they surely fall. A load carried on the head falls head down when it is thrown off. While you wait, let no hostility show.
couplets.sensitive: counsels submitting to an adversary; could reach someone being abused

couplets.plain: When what is hard to come by comes your way, do at that very moment what is hard to do.
couplets.pm: When the time that rulers bent on beating an enemy can’t obtain for themselves comes to them, they should at once, before it passes, do the deeds they couldn’t do without it. Strength can’t make such a time, it rarely comes on its own, and it runs off once it has come. So when the time comes, act fast.

links.quote: When what is hard to come by comes your way

couplets.plain: In the time for holding still, be like the heron. When your moment comes, be like its strike.
couplets.pm: When it isn’t time to move, sit still as the heron does. When the time comes, finish the work without fail, as it finishes with its strike. Waiting for a fish it stands as if lifeless, so as not to miss it, and when the fish arrives it strikes at once, before it can escape. So it serves as the image for both waiting and acting.

links.reason: Asks for the heron’s stillness while you wait and its strike when your moment comes.

links.quote: In the time for holding still, be like the heron
links.reason: The heron stands idle until the moment comes, then strikes at once.
